measures.questionText: Shall the Act be approved which provides a homestead exemption from Chattooga County ad valorem taxes for county purposes in the amount of $70,000.00 of the assessed value of the homestead for residents of that county who are 70 years of age or older and whose income does not exceed $38,000.00?

provenance.sourceOrg: Office of the Governor of Georgia
provenance.quote: Shall the Act be approved which provides a homestead exemption from Chattooga County ad valorem taxes for county purposes in the amount of $70,000.00 of the assessed value of the homestead for residents of that county who are 70 years of age or older and whose income does not exceed $38,000.00?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Exempts $70,000 of a qualifying homestead’s assessed value from Chattooga County property taxes, including county bond taxes, beginning January 1, 2027 if voters approve. The resident must be at least 70 on January 1 of the application year; the resident’s income plus that of a spouse living in the homestead must total no more than $38,000 for the preceding year, using federal adjusted gross income. It replaces other county-tax homestead exemptions and does not apply to state, school or city property taxes; assessed value above the exemption remains taxable. The resident or an agent must apply to the county tax commissioner, but recipients of the existing 2007 senior county-tax exemption would receive the new exemption without filing a new application. The exemption renews while the home remains the resident’s homestead; recipients must report loss of eligibility.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the $70,000 county-tax homestead exemption for qualifying seniors meeting the $38,000 income limit.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed replacement senior county-tax exemption.
